deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the critique of algebraic de Rham cohomology (point 5) in Grothendieck's preparatory notes for his Nov–Dec 1967 IHES lectures on crystals, published as 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' in Dix exposés, 1968.

(1) It finishes item 3° from the previous page. Even when the dimensions dim H^i_DR(X) are the right Betti numbers (e.g. for abelian varieties), the coefficient field is of characteristic p > 0 (an observation he credits to Serre). A Lefschetz fixed-point formula in H_DR therefore only gives the number of fixed points, and hence the Frobenius traces, mod p. This is not enough to determine the exact values that occur in Lefschetz formulas, nor to formulate the Weil conjectures satisfactorily. It motivates characteristic-0 coefficients: crystalline cohomology over W(k), tensored with the fraction field.

(2) Item b) is the second criticism, in characteristic 0. Classical de Rham theory, used to express the complex cohomology, is tied too exclusively to nonsingular varieties. One may of course form the complex Ω•_X of Kähler differentials and its hypercohomology for arbitrary X. But Grothendieck claims that already for a curve over C, affine or projective (e.g. a line with an ordinary double point), this does not give the correct first Betti numbers. One cannot simply restrict to nonsingular varieties: studying them forces singular varieties on us, e.g. as fibres of morphisms of smooth schemes f: X → Y.

(3) The next page draws the conclusion. One wants an algebraic description of the Leray spectral sequence of f^an. This requires coefficients more general than Ω•_X, including more general complexes of differential operators. This is the motivation for the infinitesimal site and crystals, and for Hartshorne's de Rham cohomology via formal completion of a smooth embedding.
errors:
The illustrative example seems wrong as stated, at least for the projective nodal curve.
- The node xy = 0 is quasi-homogeneous. On a graded algebra, contraction with the Euler vector field gives a homotopy (L_E = d i_E + i_E d acts as multiplication by the weight). So the Kähler de Rham complex of C[x,y]/(xy), and likewise of C{x,y}/(xy), is acyclic in positive weight; the analytic Poincaré lemma holds at an ordinary double point.
- This is consistent with K. Saito's 1971 criterion: for isolated hypersurface singularities, Ω• resolves C iff the singularity is quasi-homogeneous.
- Hence, by GAGA, a projective curve with only ordinary double points does have H^*(X, Ω•_X) of the correct dimensions.
- Genuine failures require non-quasi-homogeneous singularities.
- The affine case needs a separate algebraic-versus-analytic comparison, but there too the node is unlikely to be a counterexample.
- The general point (Kähler de Rham cohomology is wrong for singular X) is correct; the chosen example is not.

Minor: 'l'expérience apprend que' and the fibration argument are heuristic. They are not errors, but the singular-fibre example only matters once one wants relative or Leray statements, which the next page makes explicit.

ideas.what: De Rham cohomology in char p has char-p coefficients, so Lefschetz trace formulas give fixed-point counts only mod p; inadequate for the Weil conjectures
ideas.modern_name: Motivation for p-adic (crystalline / rigid) Weil cohomology with coefficients in K = Frac W(k)
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (Dix exposés, 1968), introduction

ideas.what: Kähler de Rham complex Ω•_X of a singular variety does not compute the singular cohomology of X^an
ideas.modern_name: Failure of the Poincaré lemma on singular spaces; replaced by Hartshorne's de Rham cohomology via completion, the infinitesimal site, the Du Bois complex, h-differentials
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1966-68), Hartshorne (1975), Bloom–Herrera; Saito (1971) for the quasi-homogeneous criterion
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, §§1-4 (infinitesimal site)

ideas.what: Necessity of singular varieties (as fibres of morphisms of smooth schemes) as motivation for a de Rham theory of singular schemes and relative Leray spectral sequences
ideas.modern_name: Relative de Rham / Gauss–Manin; coefficients as crystals / D-modules
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the published motivation section of the crystals lectures. Its content (char-p coefficients give only mod-p Lefschetz counts; Kähler de Rham cohomology fails for singular varieties) is well known and appears in the 1968 text. The only notable detail is that the specific example (ordinary double point) is apparently incorrect, since nodes are quasi-homogeneous. That is a small slip, not a missed result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'définition est due au cas p>0' should read 'définition est de car. p>0'. It continues 'le corps de' from the previous page: '...le corps de définition est de car p>0, et donc ils ne se prêtent pas...'.

Line 2-3: 'la détermination de nos exacts[?] de b^i[?] par formules de Lefschetz' is probably 'la détermination des vals exactes des [traces/nombres] par formules de Lefschetz (mais seulement leurs vals mod p)'.
Margin insertion after 'De Rham classique': 'pour exprimer la coh. "complexe"' (confirmed by image).
'p.ex. à droite[?] affine ou projective' is likely 'p.ex. la droite affine ou projective avec pt double ordinaire', i.e. a rational curve with a node; the struck-out text below is illegible.
'dim H_DR(X)' carries a subscript DR written below H in the image: H^1_DR(X).
